artworks.title: Alcmaeon Killing His Mother Eriphyle
artworks.description: Pompeian fresco (Naples MANN): Alcmaeon strikes down Eriphyle — the matricide for Harmonia's necklace that opens his Erinyes-driven wanderings.

artworks.title: The Erinyes Drive Alcmaeon from the Corpse of Eriphyle
artworks.description: Fuseli's Kunsthaus Zürich canvas: the Furies swarm as Alcmaeon flees Eriphyle's body — Romantic terror for the pollution that drives him through Arcadia to Achelous.

artworks.title: The Erinyes beside the Body of Eriphyle
artworks.description: Fuseli's related Louvre treatment: the Erinyes crowd Eriphyle's corpse as Alcmaeon is claimed for exile — the necklace's second harvest made visible.

popCulture.title: Alcmaeon in Psophis
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides' lost tragedy of the matricide's purification at Psophis — staged with Alcestis, it fixed Alcmaeon's exile as Attic drama.

popCulture.title: Alcmaeon in Corinth
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Produced posthumously with the Bacchae and Iphigenia in Aulis — the lost play of Alcmaeon's children and Corinthian recognition.

popCulture.title: Epigoni (play)
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' lost Epigoni framed the sons' revenge on Thebes and Alcmaeon's charge to avenge Amphiaraus on Eriphyle.
